name: Espiritu Santo Highland Forest
blurb: Fig trees, fruit doves and flying foxes in the rainforest of Vanuatu.

tip.title: Remove the fig trees
tip.text: Figs feed pigeons, doves, flying foxes and more. Set Fig trees to -100% and watch the fruit eaters, then the snake and hawk above them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Fig trees fruit heavily and are a widely used food for fruit-eating birds and bats in tropical forests.

nodes.name: Cutnut
nodes.desc: An evergreen tree of humid forests found only in Fiji and Vanuatu. Moths and bats pollinate its flowers and its seeds are edible.

nodes.name: Macaranga
nodes.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree that colonises gaps in the forest and is often recorded around Santo.

nodes.name: Tree fern
nodes.desc: A tree fern recorded often in the wetter forest, part of the layered understorey.

nodes.name: Pacific imperial pigeon
nodes.desc: A fruit-eating pigeon that feeds on many fruit species and passes seeds through undamaged, making it an important seed disperser.

nodes.name: Red-bellied fruit dove
nodes.desc: A fruit dove of lowland forest in Vanuatu, New Caledonia and the Santa Cruz Islands, and one of the most recorded birds near Santo.

nodes.name: Vanuatu flying fox
nodes.desc: A fruit bat found only in Vanuatu and listed as Vulnerable. Flying foxes are fruit and nectar eaters and are hunted for food on Santo.

nodes.name: Rainbow lorikeet
nodes.desc: Feeds on fruit, pollen and nectar with a brush-tipped tongue, and pollinates flowers such as coconut palms in Melanesia.

nodes.name: Black rat
nodes.desc: An introduced omnivore eating seeds, fruit, invertebrates and sometimes birds; it is recorded around Santo.

nodes.name: Tiger moth
nodes.desc: A moth recorded on Santo. Caterpillars of this genus are known to feed on fig leaves, and adults are prey for bats and birds.

nodes.name: Fawn leaf-nosed bat
nodes.desc: An insect-eating cave-roosting bat; it takes beetles and moths in flight close to vegetation, and is the most recorded mammal near Santo.

nodes.name: Grey fantail
nodes.desc: A small insect-catching forest bird, widely recorded around Santo.

nodes.name: Pacific kingfisher
nodes.desc: A perch-and-pounce hunter that takes insects, lizards, frogs and crabs, and is found across the South Pacific including Vanuatu.

nodes.name: Copper-tailed skink
nodes.desc: A common small Pacific skink that hunts small invertebrates on the forest floor and in clearings.

nodes.name: Pacific boa
nodes.desc: A forest snake recorded on Espiritu Santo that eats birds, lizards, rodents and bats; the island has no native land mammal predators.

nodes.name: Swamp harrier
nodes.desc: A bird of prey found in Vanuatu that eats birds, small mammals, reptiles and carrion.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Tropical sun at 15 degrees south drives year-round growth in the forest canopy.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Heavy rain on the mountains of Santo feeds the island rainforest and cloud forest.

nodes.name: Volcanic soil
nodes.desc: Soil that supplies nutrients to forest plants and is rebuilt by decomposers.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
